tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read one file, or several in ONE call via file_paths (each gets its own [FILE] section; offset/limit apply to every file in the batch) — when 2+ files are needed, batch them in a single call to save turns. A full read returns the first page under a [FILE] header (lines x-y of N); when PARTIAL is shown, page onward with offset/limit. A repeat full read of an unchanged file returns a cached stub — use offset/limit to re-read a specific slice.

file_paths.description: Batch of file paths to read in one call.

tools.doc: read_file(file_path?, file_paths?, offset?, limit?) — Read one file, or batch several via file_paths in ONE call ([FILE] sections; offset 1-based, applies per file in a batch). Full read returns first page + header; PARTIAL -> page with offset/limit; unchanged repeat -> cached stub.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Edit or create files. Mode A — targeted change: old_string -> new_string (must match exactly and uniquely; identical strings error). Mode B — create or overwrite a WHOLE file: file_path + new_string only. Mode C — batch/multi-file diff: '*** Add File: p' / '*** Update File: p' / '*** Delete File: p' / '*** Move to: p' headers, optionally wrapped in '*** Begin Patch' / '*** End Patch'. Update bodies use @@ hunks: lines prefixed '-' are removed, '+' are added, and ' ' (space) are unchanged context lines that anchor the hunk — line numbers are optional and ignored, so hunks tolerate drift (preferred over SEARCH/REPLACE for multi-hunk and multi-file edits). Applied transactionally with [OK]/[ERROR] summary. verify = 'py_compile' | 'tsc' | shell command, runs after the write.

new_string.description: Replacement (Mode A) or full file content (Mode B: omit old_string).

diff.description: Mode C payload: '*** File:' headers (optional *** Begin Patch / *** End Patch envelope) with @@ hunks — '-' removed, '+' added, ' ' context anchors; line numbers optional and ignored. Legacy SEARCH/REPLACE blocks and numbered unified diffs are also accepted.

tools.doc: edit_file(file_path, old_string?, new_string?, diff?, verify?) — A: old_string+new_string = targeted unique replace; B: new_string only = create/overwrite whole file; C: diff = '*** Add/Update/Delete/Move File' headers (optional *** Begin Patch/End Patch) with @@ hunks: '-' removed, '+' added, ' ' context anchors (numbers optional). verify=py_compile|tsc|shell after write.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a shell command (Git Bash, POSIX). Foreground blocks and streams output; server-like commands (npm run dev, vite, uvicorn, python -m http.server...) that exceed the timeout are auto-moved to background. Background runs return a process name managed via process_action. Windows tools work as subprocesses: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command '...' or cmd.exe /c '...'.

command.description: Shell command; also names the process for process_action='logs'|'kill'|'wait'.

timeout.description: Wall-clock limit in ms (default 120000, max 600000; values <1000 are seconds). Use >=60000 for installs; background=true for servers.

idle_timeout.description: Kill after this long with no output and no CPU activity, in ms (default 60000; 0 disables). Server-like/busy commands are backgrounded instead of killed.

expect.description: Regex expected in output; typed pass/fail. For background starts it is awaited up to ready_timeout.

ready_timeout.description: Background readiness wait in ms (default 15000; 0 = don't wait). Also used by process_action='ready'.

input.description: process_action='send': text written to the background process stdin.

tools.doc: run_command(command, timeout?, idle_timeout?, background?, process_action?, workdir?, expect?, tail_lines?, ready_timeout?, input?) — Git Bash (POSIX): pipes, &&, $( ), jq, gh. timeout ms (default 120000; <1000 = seconds; max 600000); idle_timeout kills commands idle by output AND CPU (default 60000; 0 = off); server-like/busy commands auto-background on timeout. process_action=list|logs|kill|wait|ready|send|kill_all. background+expect waits for readiness and reports the listening URL. workdir sets cwd, expect checks output regex.

tools.name: read_pdf
tools.description: Read text from a PDF file, optionally limited to specific pages.

page_numbers.description: Specific pages to read, e.g. '1-3,5,7-9' (overrides max_pages).

tools.doc: read_pdf(file_path, max_pages?, page_numbers?) — Read text from a PDF file.

tools.description: Create a Word document (.docx) with an optional title heading and paragraph content (one paragraph per line).

content.description: Document body — one paragraph per line.

tools.doc: create_docx(file_path, title?, content?) — Create a Word document (.docx).

tools.name: create_xlsx
tools.description: Create an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx) from headers + rows.

rows.description: Data rows (each row is an array of cell values).

tools.doc: create_xlsx(file_path, headers, rows) — Create an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx).

tools.name: search_code
tools.description: Regex-search file contents ('content', default) or match path globs ('files'). Output styles: lines (default), files (matching paths), count (matches per file). Matching lines are annotated with their enclosing symbol unless annotate=false; snippet='function' returns the enclosing function body instead of single lines. Multi-pattern results ranked via patterns=[...]. Results are workspace-relative; up to max_matches lines shown (default 100; full list saved to /scratch when exceeded). Narrow with path/glob.

pattern.description: Regex (content mode) or glob/filename fragment (files mode).

path.description: Directory or single file to search (default: workspace root).

output.description: Content answer style: matching lines, matching paths, or matches per file.

smart_case.description: Ignore case when the pattern has no uppercase letters.

fixed_strings.description: Treat the pattern as a literal string, not a regex.

context.description: Lines of context around each match (lines output).

annotate.description: Prefix each match with its enclosing symbol (default true).

snippet.description: line (default) or function: show the enclosing function body once per function.

tools.doc: search_code(pattern?, patterns?, path?, glob?, mode?, output?, ignore_case?, smart_case?, word?, fixed_strings?, context?, max_matches?, annotate?, snippet?) — Regex search (content) or filename search. output=lines|files|count; results annotated with enclosing symbol; snippet=function returns the body; up to 100 lines shown (full list in scratch).

tools.name: ast_search
tools.description: Structural search over Python files (stdlib AST, no text matching). Warehouse tool: not assigned to any agent scope yet; enable per specialist. Results are workspace-relative and bounded like search_code.

rule.description: Structural query. call/import/class_bases/decorator require name; long_function/many_params use min_lines/max_params.

name.description: Function/method/module/class/decorator name for name-based rules (dotted names allowed).

path.description: Directory or single file to search (default: workspace root).

glob.description: Comma-separated file filters, '!' excludes. Python files only.

max_params.description: many_params threshold; functions above it are reported (default 5).

tools.doc: ast_search(rule, name?, path?, glob?, min_lines?, max_params?, max_results?) — Structural search over Python (call/import/class_bases/decorator/bare_except/long_function/many_params/no_docstring).

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the caller structured questions and wait for answers. Use on material ambiguity, a decision only the caller can make, or plan approval. Each question needs 2-4 options (use multiSelect=true if more than one may apply). For plan-approval flows, set intent.kind="plan-review" on the question and put the approving option's label in intent.approve.

id.description: Stable identifier for this question. Used to reference the answer in your next reply.

header.description: Short chip label shown above the question, ≤12 chars. Example: 'Approve plan'.

options.description: 2-4 choices shown to the user. The first option is the recommended one.

multiSelect.description: true = the user can pick multiple options. false (default) = pick exactly one.

tools.doc: ask_user(questions, timeout?) — Ask the human a structured question and wait for the answer (use when the request is ambiguous, a decision is needed, or a plan needs approval via plan-review intent).

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Browser automation: navigate, click, fill, type, press, extract, screenshot, close. Selector = CSS or @ref from the navigate snapshot. Start servers with run_command(background=true) first.
tools.doc: browser_act(action, selector?, text?, key?, what?, path?) — click / fill / type / press / extract / screenshot / close.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Open a URL in a headless Chromium browser and return the page content as an accessibility snapshot with @ref selectors. Handles JavaScript-rendered pages, SPAs, complex web apps. Returns interactive element tree for use with other browser tools. Slower than a plain GET but handles everything.

url.description: The full URL to navigate to.

wait_ms.description: Optional. Milliseconds to wait for page load (default 5000).

tools.doc: browser_navigate(url, wait_ms?) — Open URL in headless Chromium, returns snapshot with @ref selectors.

tools.name: browser_extract
tools.description: Extract content from the current browser page. Use after browser_navigate. Can extract text, HTML, attribute values, page title, or URL. Uses @ref selectors from the accessibility snapshot.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector or @ref from snapshot. Empty = entire page.

tools.doc: browser_extract(what?, selector?) — Extract text/html/value from current browser page.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current browser page. Saves to a temp file and returns the path. Use for visual verification of pages.

path.description: Optional file path to save the screenshot. Auto-named if empty.

tools.doc: browser_screenshot(path?) — Screenshot of current browser page.

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Close the current browser session and free all resources (memory, Chrome process). Call when done with web research to avoid resource leaks.
tools.doc: browser_close() — Close browser session and free resources.

tools.name: look_at_screen
tools.description: Capture the user's live screen RIGHT NOW and attach it inline (vision). Use when the answer depends on what the user is currently viewing: a highlighted passage, a chart, a page, an error, or when they say 'this'/'here'/'what I'm looking at'. Turns the overlay's screen sharing on if it is off. The frame reaches you as an image before your next reply.
tools.doc: look_at_screen() — Capture the user's live screen now and attach it inline (vision). For 'this'/'here'/highlighted content questions; enables sharing if off.

tools.name: set_screen_share
tools.description: Change the live overlay's screen-sharing mode: 'on' (preview + one fresh frame attached to each voice turn), 'off' (stop sharing), 'continuous' (also refresh the latest frame every few seconds so look_at_screen is near-real-time). Ask the user before turning 'continuous' on; turn it off when the task is done.
tools.doc: set_screen_share(mode) — Live screen sharing: on / off / continuous (continuous refreshes every few seconds for near-real-time look_at_screen).

tools.name: update_feature
tools.description: Add or update a feature entry in long-term project memory (features.md) after a feature is implemented. file_refs is a list of {"path", "lines", "purpose"} objects.

tools.name: update_project_meta
tools.description: Add/update a project metadata section in long-term memory (project.md). Only these keys are allowed: Tech Stack, Frontend, Database, Testing, Architecture, Project Type, Goals.

key.description: Metadata key (Tech Stack, Frontend, Database, Testing, Architecture, Project Type, Goals).

tools.name: github_apply_gate
tools.description: Create a repo and/or install the tiered CI/security gate: T1 fast-checks / T2 staging / T3 release workflows + .harness-ci.json, dev/staging/prod branch ladder, waits for first run, enforces prod branch protection. Non-destructive otherwise; stack auto-detected. Confirms first (gate=ask).

update_levels.description: Re-render level-owned files after a branch rename.

tools.doc: github_apply_gate(repo, stack?, codeql_on?, create?, private?, description?, gate?) — The ONE gate tool: create the repo (create=True) and/or install the security/perf gate (seed + branch protection). Confirms with the user (gate: ask|yes|no).

tools.name: create_coding_project
tools.description: Create a NEW project: creates the folder (under D:\MyProject, or under parent_root if given), registers it as a workspace with its own chat, and assigns a durable Dev agent to it. Use ONLY when the user genuinely asks for a new project. NEVER call this for work on an existing project. Pass wait=false when creating SEVERAL projects in one burst — their first Dev turns run in parallel in the background. The DFD agent MUST pass parent_root (the client folder under D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects) so client projects always live inside the client root.

name.description: Project/folder name. 1-64 chars; filesystem-safe — avoid '/', '\\', '..', control characters, and leading dots. Use kebab-case or snake_case.

concept.description: The user's concept/goal for the project; the Dev agent starts from this.

wait.description: Wait for the Dev's first turn before returning. Use false for multi-project bursts.

parent_root.description: Optional parent folder. DFD agent: the client folder under D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects (enforced to stay inside it). Others: leave empty.

tools.doc: create_coding_project(name, concept, wait?, parent_root?) — Create a NEW project: folder (D:\MyProject, or parent_root for the DFD agent) + workspace + chat + durable Dev. Only for genuinely new projects. wait=false for bursts. DFD agent passes parent_root inside D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Maintain the plan dock. Call when jobs change (spawn, progress, abort). FULL REPLACEMENT each call: send every step with its current status; at most one in_progress. Settled jobs use status=completed — put the reason in the step text when not successful. For small tweaks use ops instead of resending everything (mutually exclusive with plan): [{op, match?, step?, status?}] with op=add (needs step) | set_status (needs match+status) | rename (needs match+step) | remove (needs match); match is a case-insensitive substring of the step text.

explanation.description: Short note shown above the plan (e.g. 'Spawned 3 jobs, waiting for results'). Keep to one line.

match.description: Case-insensitive substring of the step text (set_status/rename/remove).

step.description: Step text (add, or rename's new text).
Short, human-readable job description. For settled jobs, prefix the reason when not successful (e.g. 'Build snake game — failed: tests did not pass').

tools.doc: update_plan(explanation?, plan?, ops?) — Maintain the task plan. FULL replacement: always send every step (at most one in_progress), or patch small tweaks via ops=[{op: add|set_status|rename|remove, match?, step?, status?}] (mutually exclusive with plan).

tools.name: delegate
tools.description:
Spawn one or more workspace agents (Developer / General / House) IN PARALLEL. Every item gets its own visible chat; final replies arrive as [DELEGATION RESULT] events while you keep coordinating.

BRIEF — you define WHAT, never HOW. Each item carries outcome (what the user gets when it is done, in the user's terms) and acceptance (how success will be judged — observable evidence). Never prescribe libraries, frameworks, architecture, step lists, file-by-file plans, or design direction; the specialist is the pro and owns the method (it may deviate and must report deviations). Name a command in acceptance only if the user named it or it is the project's standard entry point; otherwise describe the behavior and let the specialist choose the proof. One or two lines each — if they get long, you are doing the specialist's job. Method reminders are added to the task automatically; do not write them yourself.

BATCHING — per user turn: put EVERY independent job from the current request into a SINGLE delegate(items=[...]) call. Any agent mix is allowed and runs in parallel — solo scope (just Developer, just General, or just House) or mixed (Developer + General, Developer + House, all three). The sole batching criterion is independence. If job B needs job A's output, do NOT bundle B with A: delegate A first, wait for its [DELEGATION RESULT], then delegate B with A's result in the task. Never split a single request across multiple delegate calls for tidiness or sequencing — one call, all independent items.

EFFORT — match effort to the request: one job for a simple ask, 2-4 for comparisons, more ONLY when directions are truly independent. Jobs beyond the parallel cap wait as 'queued' and start automatically — never flood the system.

RESULTS — each job's final reply arrives as a [DELEGATION RESULT] summary (plus its artifact path and, when set, acceptance). Drill into the full report with delegation_status(id=...) when needed; never paste reports into your reply.

CHAT CONTINUATION — chat_id is optional. Omit it for a new job (default). Set it ONLY when this item is a follow-up, correction, or bug on a chat you can identify from a prior [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session. If the chat_id you pass does not exist, the runtime silently starts a new chat — so never guess an id.

RESUME — project continues a REGISTERED project's durable Dev session instead of starting a new chat. When the request is a follow-up, bug fix, or new work on an EXISTING project and you have no chat_id from a prior [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session, pass project=<name> (agent must be Dev or omitted) instead of workspace/chat_id. The message goes to the project's durable Dev in its own project chat — nothing new is created — and the completion arrives as a [DELEGATION RESULT] like any other job. Unknown names return [NOT FOUND] with the available names — never guess. Omit project for genuinely new work.

agent.description: Target workspace agent. Developer builds/fixes software; General handles research, docs, images, personal notes/admin; House controls smart-home devices. Case-insensitive.

task.description: Complete, self-contained instruction: goal, relevant paths/targets, constraints. The agent sees only this text. Context, not method — do not prescribe step-by-step process (use outcome/acceptance for the WHAT).

outcome.description: What the user gets when this job is done — the visible result, in the user's terms, 1-2 sentences. WHAT, never HOW: no libraries, frameworks, architecture, step lists, or design direction. Real paths the user named are fine as targets; invented ones are not.

acceptance.description: How success will be judged — observable evidence (a behavior, a result, something that must exist or respond). Not internals. Name a command only if the user named it or it is the project's standard entry point. The specialist chooses how to meet and prove it.

timeout.description: Wall-clock seconds before the job is aborted and marked FAILED (default 3600; 0 = no limit). Fresh jobs only.

title.description: Short label for the delegation chat (e.g. 'Space game · Dev').

chat_id.description: Omit for a new chat. Set ONLY with a chat_id surfaced by an earlier [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session — never guess. Unknown ids silently start a new chat.

project.description: Registered project name (fuzzy match, e.g. 'my-app'). Set this INSTEAD of workspace/chat_id to continue the project's durable Dev session in its own project chat — no new tab is created. Only with agent Dev (or omitted).

workspace.description: Workspace id, folder path, or name. Omit to use the default: current project for Dev, General workspace for General, House workspace for House.

images.description: Absolute file paths of image attachments relevant to THIS item. Missing files are silently dropped, so only attach paths you have verified exist.

items.task: Build a snake game in Python with tests
items.title: Snake game · Dev
items.outcome: A playable snake game that starts with one command and keeps a high score.
items.acceptance: The game starts and is playable; the project's test command passes.

items.task: Turn off the living room lights
items.title: Lights off · House
items.acceptance: The living room light reports power=off.

items.task: Save a journal note: shipped v0.1
items.title: Note · General
items.outcome: The note is saved in the journal.
items.acceptance: Searching the journal for 'shipped v0.1' finds the note.

items.task: Fix the login crash (regression from PR #42)
items.title: Login crash fix
items.acceptance: Logging in with valid credentials reaches the home screen; the project's test command passes.

items.task: Fix the login crash on the settings screen and add a regression test
items.title: Login crash fix

tools.doc: delegate(items=[{agent, task, outcome?, acceptance?, timeout?, title?, chat_id?, project?, workspace?, images?}]) — Spawn Developer/General/House agents; each gets its own chat (project=<name> continues a registered project's durable Dev in its own chat instead). outcome/acceptance define WHAT success is — never method. Results arrive as [DELEGATION RESULT] summaries + artifact paths; drill in with delegation_status(id).

tools.name: delegation_status
tools.description: List all delegations spawned this session with live statuses (queued / running / done / failed / cancelled) and their chat ids. Call when you need to know what is still outstanding — typically before a wrap-up summary, after a long wait, or when you are unsure whether everything has settled. Pass id for ONE job's full evidence bundle (task, outcome, acceptance, full report, recent chat, file digest); wait_seconds (0-300) waits briefly for a job first; status filters the board.

id.description: Job id (del-xxxx) for the full evidence bundle of one job. Omit for the board.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this long for a job before answering (default 0 = answer now).

status.description: Board filter: only show jobs in this state.

tools.doc: delegation_status(id?, wait_seconds?, status?) — Board of this session's delegations (queued/running/done/failed/cancelled) with chats and elapsed time; id=<del-id> drills into one job's full evidence (task, outcome, acceptance, full artifact report, recent chat, file digest).

tools.name: job_message
tools.description: Steer a RUNNING delegation mid-flight when the user adds scope or changes direction. Fresh jobs: mirrored into the job chat + queued on its steering channel. Resume jobs: queued on the durable Dev child (FIFO). Only works while the job is running — otherwise delegate a follow-up. Never blocks.

job_id.description: Job id (del-xxxx) from delegate or delegation_status.

message.description: Steering message: the added scope or direction change.

tools.doc: job_message(job_id, message) — Steer a RUNNING delegation mid-flight (fresh: steering channel; resume: durable Dev FIFO). Running jobs only; never blocks.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel ONE running delegation when the user says stop. Fresh jobs: cooperative abort of the job chat. Resume jobs: interrupt of the durable Dev child. Settles the entry as CANCELLED and reports back as a [DELEGATION RESULT]. Already-settled jobs are a no-op.

job_id.description: Job id (del-xxxx) from delegate or delegation_status.

reason.description: One-clause reason shown in the wrap-up (default: cancelled by the user).

tools.doc: job_cancel(job_id, reason?) — Cancel ONE running delegation (fresh: abort; resume: interrupt). Reports back as [DELEGATION RESULT] CANCELLED.

tools.name: call_subagent
tools.description: Specialist subagent lifecycle (see Subagents list). action=run: spawn and block until the final report (default). action=spawn: start it in the background and keep working on other parts, then collect with status. action=status: status + latest result of a spawned child (wait_seconds≤300). action=message: steer a running child (queued) or send a follow-up. action=stop: interrupt a running child. action=list: this session's subagents. Prefer spawn+status for deep/long verification so you are not blocked.

name.description: Subagent type from the Subagents list, e.g. UI | DevOps. Required for run/spawn.

task.description: Goal + targets (files/URL/repo) + acceptance check + constraints. Context, not method — do not prescribe design direction or step-by-step process. Required for run/spawn.

child_id.description: Spawned child id (from action=spawn) for status/message/stop.

wait_seconds.description: For status: poll up to this many seconds (max 300) before returning.

tools.doc: call_subagent(name, task, action?, child_id?, message?, wait_seconds?) — Specialist subagent lifecycle: run (block) / spawn (background) / status / message / stop / list (e.g. UI for browser verification).

tools.name: files_changed
tools.description: Stage 5 (advisory): list the most recent external file changes in the active workspace. The agent can call this to notice when the user (or another tool outside this run) edits a file. Does NOT invalidate the read cache or interrupt a running tool. Requires the optional `watchfiles` package; if not installed, returns a friendly 'not available' string.

tools.doc: house_set_device(device_id, state) — Actuate a device: light {power,brightness,colorTemp}, thermostat {targetTemp,mode}, lock {locked}, plug {power}, blinds {position}, camera {recording}. Sensors read-only.

tools.name: create_client
tools.description: Create a client scaffold under D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects\<slug>\ (client.json + progress.md + mem/). REQUIRES explicit owner approval first (approved_by must be set). Never call without approval.

business_name.description: Client business name (slugified to folder name).

vertical.description: One of: fnb, salon, laundry, klinik, gym, bimbel, bengkel, beauty, travel, property, katering, photo.

approved_by.description: Who approved this scaffold (must be non-empty; the DFD agent sets it after owner approval).

order_id.description: DFD order id this client belongs to (optional).

tools.doc: create_client(business_name, vertical, features?, whatsapp?, domain?, approved_by?, order_id?) — Create client scaffold under D:\MyProject\DFDClientProjects\<slug>\ (client.json + progress.md + mem/). REQUIRES explicit owner approval (approved_by).

tools.name: create_group
tools.description: Start a durable project that keeps working until it is done, across sessions and restarts, with its own folder, agents, tasks and board. Use when the goal is genuinely durable and multi-step. Do NOT use for a single self-contained request or for recurring work. Pass structured milestones and members — do not hand-write a manifest. Returns the project id and folder path; the effects are queued, so follow progress with group_board.

goal.description: The outcome wanted, one or two sentences.

milestones.description: Ordered phases. Each: {id, title, depends_on?, items:[{id, title, detail, acceptance:[...]}]}. Every item MUST have at least one acceptance criterion or it can never be completed.

members.description: Agents for this project. Each: {name, derived_from, model?, thinking?, tools?, skills?, mcp?}. Omit entirely for a single-agent project (the orchestrator does the work).

autonomy.description: Permission envelope, enforced. project_folder / external_read / external_write / destructive: autonomous | needs_approval | blocked. Work inside the project folder is always free; anything outside follows external_write, and needs_approval means the member parks and waits for the owner rather than failing — tell the owner that an outside action will need their approval. Also run_command: never | blocked | autonomous — never (the default) removes the shell from every member's toolset entirely, while blocked offers it and refuses dangerous commands at runtime. Set run_command to blocked or autonomous only for projects that genuinely need builds or tests; a member holding a shell can reach outside the project folder.

budget_usd.description: Hard spend ceiling. Enforced, not advisory.

deadline.description: ISO timestamp after which dispatch halts.

skills.description: Skill names to copy into the project.

mcp.description: MCP servers to attach (must already be installed on this machine).

project_id.description: Optional folder slug; otherwise derived from the goal.

tools.doc: create_group(goal, milestones, members?, autonomy?, completion?, budget_usd?, deadline?, skills?, mcp?, project_id?) — Start a durable project that runs until done, across restarts. Create only when the goal is genuinely durable; the orchestrator decides with high reasoning. Every item needs acceptance criteria. Queued; follow with group_board.

tools.name: group_board
tools.description: Read a project's current state: milestones, items, statuses, spend, and anything waiting on a human. Use to answer 'what is left?' or 'why is this stuck?'. Read-only and immediate — it does not wait for a tick.
tools.doc: group_board(project_id) — Milestones, items, statuses, spend, and what is waiting on a human. Read-only, immediate.

tools.name: group_item_detail
tools.description: One item in full: status, attempts, latest result, and its acceptance criteria. Use when the board shows something blocked or failed and you need the reason.
tools.doc: group_item_detail(project_id, item_id) — One item in full: attempts, latest result, and its acceptance criteria (why it passed or failed).

tools.name: group_events
tools.description: A project's event log in order — every state change, who made it, and when. Use to explain what happened while the user was away, or to trace a decision.

since.description: Only events after this seq (for polling).

tools.doc: group_events(project_id, since?, limit?) — The project's event log in order: every state change, actor, and time. Use to explain what happened while the user was away.

tools.name: group_update
tools.description: Change a RUNNING project. One op per call, applied by the supervisor on its next tick (~15s), writing exactly one event. ops: add_item, add_milestone, invalidate_item, cancel_item, add_member, remove_member, attach_tool, attach_mcp, detach_mcp, attach_skill, detach_skill, pause, resume, close. 'invalidate_item' means the PLAN was wrong — not that the work failed; it does not count as a retry. Use it when a member reports an assumption turned out to be false. Read the result back with group_board.

params.description: Op arguments: e.g. {item_id, reason} for invalidate_item; {milestone_id, title, detail, acceptance} for add_item; {name, derived_from} for add_member; {server} for attach_mcp.

tools.doc: group_update(project_id, op, params?) — Change a RUNNING project: add_item, add_milestone, invalidate_item, cancel_item, add_member, remove_member, attach_tool, attach_mcp, detach_mcp, attach_skill, detach_skill, pause, resume, close. One op per call; queued until the next supervisor tick (~15s). invalidate_item = the PLAN was wrong, not that work failed.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description: Create a time-triggered wake for THIS orchestrator chat. When due, it appends a scheduled message and wakes the orchestrator even if the user has not spoken. Use for one-off alarms ('check the agents at 3pm') and recurring checks. This is the only way to create a schedule; there is no manual task UI.

at.description: ISO timestamp or HH:MM for the first run.

prompt.description: Instruction delivered to the orchestrator; defaults to name.

tools.doc: schedule(action?, name?, at?, prompt?, recurrence?, schedule_id?) — Create/list/cancel a time-triggered wake for this orchestrator chat. When due it appends a scheduled message and wakes the orchestrator. recurrence: none|daily|weekly|monthly|interval-<minutes>. No manual task UI.

tools.name: give_note
tools.description: Create or maintain a sticky note for a chat or group project. Notes are orchestrator-owned memory and UI checklists, not work items. Use todos for a checklist. Target is chat:<id> or group:<id>; omit it to use this chat.
tools.doc: give_note(action?, target?, title?, body?, todos?, note_id?) — Orchestrator-owned sticky note/checklist for chat:<id> or group:<id>. Actions create/update/remove/list. Notes are memory, not work items.

tools.name: canvas_mode
tools.description: Watch selected agent chats and wake the orchestrator when one finishes or fails. The orchestrator can choose one chat, several, or all agent chats. While active, a completion arrives as [CANVAS EVENT]; use canvas_mode read for the work snapshot and canvas_mode message to send a follow-up to a watched chat. Exit when done. This reads work state, never card coordinates.
tools.doc: canvas_mode(action?, mode?, targets?, wake_on?, max_actions?, until?, target?, message?) — Watch agent chats (single/multiple/all) and wake the orchestrator on completion/failure. available lists selectable chats/groups; read returns the work snapshot; message sends follow-up to a watched chat; exit stops watching.

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run a short JavaScript program that calls Stark tools directly. Use this for multi-step coding work: read or search several files, compute over the results, edit files, run commands, and return one compact result. Tool calls are synchronous: const text = tools.read_file({file_path: 'src/lib.rs'}); use JSON.parse(text) for structured output. Use search('query') to discover available tools. Programs have no filesystem, network, process, or import access except through tools. Not available in plan mode. Default limits: 30s, 50 tool calls, 32KB result.

code.description: JavaScript function body. Use return to send a JSON-serializable result.

tools.doc: run_code(code, timeout_ms?, max_tool_calls?) — Run a restricted JavaScript program that calls Stark tools. Use tools.<name>({...}) synchronously and return one compact value.

tools.name: agent
tools.description: Durable three-level agent control. spawn creates or reuses a workspace agent (or a subagent from a workspace agent) with a persisted mailbox task; list/status/send/report manage the tree. The server supervisor leases and runs agents, so work survives restarts and parent chats wake on results.

agent.description: Agent role, e.g. Developer, General, House, DFD, UI.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace id when the orchestrator spawns a workspace agent.

workspace_path.description: Target workspace path when the orchestrator spawns a workspace agent.

tools.doc: agent(action, kind?, agent?, task?, title?, workspace_id?, workspace_path?, agent_id?, message?, quiet?, wait_seconds?) — Durable spawn/list/status/send/report for orchestrator → workspace → subagent.
